title.narrative: Support to the Sustainability and Equity of Public Transport Project

description.narrative: The project supports three components that will be essential to support the sustainability of the bus transport system in Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires (AMBA): (i) provision of demand-side subsidies to public transport users through the national government's social fare program and integrated fare system, (ii) institutional strengthening activities, and (iii) project management activities.Component 1: Social Fare Program and Integrated Fare System a. Sub-Component 1: Provides bus fare subsidies for eligible public transport users through Argentina's national government's social fare program, extending the program to additional vulnerable beneficiaries and localities.b. Sub-Component 1.2: Finances the "Boleto Integrado" integrated fare system, which offers discounts for multi-stage trips within the first two hours of initial boarding time, to prevent a partial mode shift towards private vehicles and reduce emissions.Component 2: Institutional strengthening. This component will finance the design and implementation of activities supporting policy and institutional transformations.a. Sub-component 2.1: Improved targeting of the social fare program - Develop a new eligibility criterion to target low-income public transport users and optimize the program's subsidy allocation.b. Sub-component 2.2: Optimization of the bus system supply - Design a new framework for bus route tendering in the AMBA, including optimizing bus routes, developing an innovative strategy for the bus market, and implementing a beneficiary feedback mechanism.c. Sub-component 2.3: Improvement of Metropolitan Transport Governance - Strengthen the existing Metropolitan Transport Agency and establish a new Metropolitan Transport Authority with clear operational mandates, a permanent budget, and dedicated staff.d. Sub-component 2.4: Strengthening public transport inclusion - Introduce a smartcard for individuals with disabilities who use public transport. Expand the harassment reporting system to new localities and provide training to bus drivers and bus inspectors on how to recognize and respond to harassment.f. Sub-component 2.5: Climate Change mitigation and adaptation in bus transport - Assess scenarios and alternatives for transitioning to low-emission vehicles in the public bus fleet of AMBA and create contingency plans for extreme weather events in bus public transport planning.Component 3. Project Management. This component includes monitoring and evaluation, audits, and verification of PBCs' achievement. The Project will contribute to climate mitigation by shifting from GHG-intensive modes to low-carbon public transport. The program is expected to retain users in the public transport system, helping offset the impacts of increasing motorization. Additionally, optimizing public transport in an efficient, accessible, and inclusive manner is a tool to improve service quality and mitigate the risk of modal shift.The Project will support gender equality by increasing women's access to public transport and broader economic and social opportunities. While women in AMBA tend to travel less, they use public transport more frequently, often making more complex trips with a greater number of non-work-related journeys and non-peak hour commutes. Women make up about 80 percent of the beneficiaries of the social fare in Argentina bus transport.The Project will support the introduction of a smartcard for persons with disabilities who use public transport. Persons with disabilities can access the system at no cost by presenting their accreditation to the bus operator without using the SUBE smartcard. To make individuals with disabilities more visible and measurable and to better understand their mobility patterns, a new dedicated smartcard will be introduced, allowing them to continue traveling for free as guaranteed by Argentine law.
To improve the affordability of bus public transport for vulnerable populations in Argentina and the sustainability of the bus public transport system in the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires.

comment.narrative: The latest monitoring data (October 2024–September 2025) show 1.35 billion trips, which remains above both the March 2025 and March 2026 targets.

title.narrative: Cost recovery ratio in national jurisdiction lines of the Metropolitan Area of Buenos Aires

comment.narrative: The indicator increased from 20 percent at baseline to 31 percent in September 2025, exceeding the intermediate target of 27 percent. The latest figure reflects subsequent adjustments in subsidies and operating costs.

title.narrative: Demand-side subsidy as a share of total subsidies

comment.narrative: The current value exceeds the March 2025 PBC target of 32 percent and is already above the March 2026 target of 37 percent. The increase reflects a policy shift away from supply-side subsidies and towards demand-side support for social fare users. The ratio is expected to stabilize as the revised cost structure for operators is implemented.
